_comment: Action dispatch for cn04-2fe56bfb, read from source on 15-Sep-2026. Line numbers are anchors checked by scripts/test_dispatch_tables.py. This is the object-dependent-verb game - see docs/trace-findings/2026-09-15-cn04-object-dependent-verb.md.

guards.meaning: level-complete flag from a previous step: advances the level, dispatches nothing.
the action budget is exhausted: the run is lost, nothing is dispatched.

available_actions.note: cn04 does NOT pass available_actions to super().__init__ (:824), so the declared set is an arcengine default that is not in this repo. The observed list is taken from every row of f714032e-914d-4bb5-bc95-386dfacebca0 and is [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]. Recorded as measured rather than asserted.

runtime_filter.meaning: Cn04._get_valid_actions is a two-way switch: while a part is held it offers ACTION1-5 intersected with _available_actions (:1171); otherwise it defers to super() (:1173), which supplies the click targets. So ACTION5 is only offered while something is selected.

calls.role: cycle the held part's sprite stack
reject the click - the held part has a stack but the click missed its anchor cell

ACTION6.effect: Clicks a cell. Resolves the cell through the camera at :1043, finds the first visible sprite covering it at :1047-1051, and then branches on whether that sprite is the one already held (:1053). Clicking the held part cycles its sprite stack; clicking a different part selects it.

branch_conditions.meaning: only visible sprites can be hit.
the clicked sprite is the one already held - this is the branch that makes ACTION6 two different verbs.
the held part has more than one sprite in its stack; otherwise the click is rejected at :1063.
the click landed on the part's own anchor cell; otherwise rejected at :1061.
the held part has a single-entry stack: the click on it is rejected outright.

calls.role: step the held part through its sprite stack
re-place the part after the change

ACTION5.effect: THE object-dependent verb. ACTION5 is a rotation on a part whose sprite stack has one entry and an EXTENT CHANGE on a part whose stack has more. The whole difference is the length test at :1070. A part that has not been fully expanded carries fewer marks than its expanded form, so marks that must be satisfied are absent from the board until it is expanded. Guarded at :1068 - with nothing held, ACTION5 does nothing.

branch_conditions.meaning: nothing is held: ACTION5 falls straight through to :1079 and changes nothing.
stack length > 1 steps the part up its stack (extent change); the else at :1072 rotates 90 degrees instead. This is the branch the whole finding rests on.
if the change completes the level the win flag is set and the step returns early.

ACTION5.note: The brief's worked example cites ':1070' for the step and ':1072' for the rotate. Those are the branch lines; the calls are at :1071 and :1073. Both forms are recorded here so a citation is unambiguous.

unhandled_actions.note: ACTION7 and RESET have no branch in Cn04.step. ACTION7 was not offered in the recording; RESET is handled by arcengine, which is vendored, and was used 5 times in the recording. RESET is now citable: arcengine IS vendored at vendor/arcengine-0.9.3/ and the `engine` block below carries its citation. sibling_builds.reason: cn04-65d47d14 appears in published-replays.json but has no directory under docs/static/games/src/, so the dispatch regions cannot be diffed at all. Runs on cn04-65d47d14 therefore cannot produce an acceptance-meeting record, and a record on one build must not cite the other's line numbers - see dispatch/README.md, where three measurable sibling pairs all show citations failing to transfer. The live-build rule (649e53a) independently excludes cn04-65d47d14 from corpus scope, so the missing source costs nothing that was eligible anyway.

notes: The ACTION1-4 arm shares one `elif` at :1080 listing all four, then re-tests inside at :1089-:1096. The branch line recorded per action is the inner test, which is the line that actually distinguishes them.
cn04 declares no available_actions; the offered set here is measured from the recording, not read from source.

engine.note: RESET is dispatched by the ENGINE, before this game's step() is reached. It is never listed in available_actions and is always accepted. Cited into vendor/arcengine-0.9.3/, the pinned sdist -- see vendor/README.md for the provenance chain and for the scope limit, which is that 0.9.3 is the only arcengine ever published and it is NOT verifiable from here that three.arcprize.org runs this build.

calls.role: the interception - the engine handles RESET at the top of execute_action, before _set_action and before this game's step() loop
the fork: a full reset only at action_count 0 or after a WIN
primary effect - every RESET after the first scoring action on a level is a LEVEL reset: the run keeps its progress and only the current level is rebuilt
the level is replaced by a clone of its clean, unplayed copy
set_level re-runs the per-level setup hook, which is what restores any per-level allowance the game grants in on_set_level
the hook itself - each game's on_set_level override runs here

branch_conditions.meaning: an env override that forces level resets; not set on the hosted service as far as any recording shows, since row 0 of every first-party recording reports full_reset true.
THE fork. _action_count is zeroed by set_level (:161) and by full_reset (:321), so 'action_count == 0' means no scoring action has been taken on the current level.

RESET.effect: RESET rebuilds the current level from its clean copy and re-runs the game's on_set_level hook (:205 -> :305 -> :326 -> :328 -> :164). It restores the level's opening arrangement AND any per-level allowance the game sets in that hook -- a step budget, a lives counter -- because the hook is re-entered, not patched. It is a FULL reset, discarding run progress, only when no action has been taken on the level or the game is already won (:313).

not_counted_as_an_action_by_the_engine.meaning: _set_action skips the action-count increment for RESET, so RESET is free against ARCBaseGame._action_count. NOTE THAT THIS IS NOT THE SESSION API'S COUNTER: every first-party recording reconciles only when RESET rows ARE counted as actions -- ls20 reports 561 actions over 562 rows containing 3 non-boot RESETs, where _action_count would give 558. Two different counters; the reconcile rule in datasets/decision-steps/README.md describes the API's.
